original_value: We propose SignFi to recognize sign language gestures using WiFi. SignFi uses Channel State Information (CSI) measured by WiFi packets as the input and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) as the classification algorithm. Existing WiFi-based sign gesture recognition technologies are tested on no more than 25 gestures that only involve hand and/or finger gestures. SignFi is able to recognize 276 sign gestures, which involve the head, arm, hand, and finger gestures, with high accuracy. SignFi collects CSI measurements to capture wireless signal characteristics of sign gestures. Raw CSI measurements are pre-processed to remove noises and recover CSI changes over sub-carriers and sampling time. Pre-processed CSI measurements are fed to a 9-layer CNN for sign gesture classification. We collect CSI traces and evaluate SignFi in the lab and home environments. There are 8,280 gesture instances, 5,520 from the lab and 2,760 from the home, for 276 sign gestures in total. For 5-fold cross validation using CSI traces of one user, the average recognition accuracy of SignFi is 98.01%, 98.91%, and 94.81% for the lab, home, and lab+home environment, respectively. We also run tests using CSI traces from 5 different users in the lab environment. The average recognition accuracy of SignFi is 86.66% for 7,500 instances of 150 sign gestures performed by 5 different users.

result.paraphrase: SignFi is a WiFi-based system for recognizing sign language gestures. It takes Channel State Information (CSI) from WiFi packets as input and uses a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for classification. Unlike existing WiFi sign-gesture recognition methods, which are evaluated on no more than 25 gestures limited to hand and/or finger movements, SignFi recognizes 276 sign gestures involving the head, arm, hand, and finger with high accuracy. It captures wireless-signal characteristics through CSI measurements, then preprocesses the raw CSI to remove noise and recover CSI changes across sub-carriers and sampling time. The processed CSI is fed into a 9-layer CNN for gesture classification. We collected CSI traces and evaluated SignFi in both lab and home environments, with 8,280 gesture instances in total: 5,520 from the lab and 2,760 from home, covering 276 sign gestures. Using 5-fold cross validation on one user's CSI traces, SignFi achieves average recognition accuracies of 98.01% in the lab, 98.91% at home, and 94.81% in the combined lab+home setting. We also tested CSI traces from five different users in the lab, where the average recognition accuracy was 86.66% for 7,500 instances of 150 sign gestures performed by those users.
